statements: Create bracket.mjs at the workspace root: an ES module with one named function export, seedBracket(entrants). Use Node.js built-ins only and no dependencies. Tests, if you write any, go under test/.

entrants lists the entries of a single-elimination tournament in seed order: index 0 is seed 1, index 1 is seed 2, and so on. Checks run in this order, the first failure decides: entrants is not an array, TypeError code 'E_TYPE'; an entry is neither a string nor a finite number, the same error; fewer than 2 entries, RangeError code 'E_COUNT'; a repeated entry, RangeError code 'E_DUPLICATE'.

Entries are compared only by strict equality, never sorted, converted or normalised: the number 1 and the string '1' are different entries, and 0 and -0 are the same entry. Entries are returned exactly as given.

With n entries the bracket size is the smallest power of two that is at least n. Seeds above n do not exist. The result is an array of size divided by 2 first-round slots; each slot is an array of two items: the entry of the better (lower numbered) seed, then the entry of the worse seed, or null when that worse seed does not exist (a bye).
Treat the bracket as having all size seeds: the two seeds of every slot add up to size plus 1.
If the better seed won every match, then in every round the two seeds that meet add up to the number of players still in that round plus 1.

Seed 1 is in the first slot. When there are at least 2 slots, the better seeds of the j-th slot from the start and of the j-th slot from the end are consecutive seed numbers 2k-1 and 2k for some k. In the first half of the slots, whenever two groups of slots feed the same later match, the group holding the better seed comes first.
The function is pure: no I/O, no shared state, the input is not mutated, and a new array is returned.
brief: Implement bracket.mjs exactly as the numbered statements specify, then stop. Do not change any other file except tests under test/.
